producer_report.summary: Added the reader-question rule `reading::check_reader_question` (new `reading/questions.rs`), run as the first `step!` in `refusing_check`. `read_for` reaches it through `check_reading_acceptance` right after `build_reading`. `check_reading_text` (replay, `athena check-reading`) and the refusal corpus use the same step. A question is accepted only if it begins `User:` (shared normalisation via the new `admission::is_user_addressed`; `Host:` and `Username:` are refused), does not say the code answers it, has at least two distinct alternatives labelled `(a)`/`(b)` or `(1)`/`(2)`, and ends with `Default:` naming one of those labels. A label counts only at the start of the text or after whitespace or `:`, so `file(s)` is not a label. The refusal lists every gap, quotes the question, and gives the repair: settle it from the repository or defaults and leave `question` null, or write `User:` + decision + labelled alternatives + `Default: (a)`, with an example. The doc comment states the refusal-rate increase is intended, with the reason and `expected 3% of newly refused readings`. A 12th `READING_RULES` line in the reader brief teaches the form, so the first question is normally valid. The brief is outside the reader token budget, so no prompt file changed. Existing gate-reaching reading tests now use a shared `VALID_QUESTION`. There are new unit tests, 17 corpus cases, and corpus tests for wiring, declared share and docs. CHANGELOG.md and docs/design/job-planning.md are updated.

criteria_check.criterion: crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs (or a new file under crates/athena-core/src/reading/) holds a reader-question rule, wired into build_reading, that gives a finding for a question that does not begin with `User:` (same prefix normalisation as admission::has_addressee), offers fewer than two concrete alternatives, or names no default the job runs on if unanswered. A Grep for the rule's function name finds its definition and its call site.
criteria_check.evidence: Grep `check_reader_question`: definition `pub fn check_reader_question(` in crates/athena-core/src/reading/questions.rs; call site `step!(check_reader_question(reading));` as the first step in `refusing_check` in reading/checks.rs. `read_for` runs `check_reading_acceptance` straight after `build_reading`. The rule is called from refusing_check rather than inside build_reading, because the corpus rule forbids other call sites and replay needs it. `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus reader_question_check_is_wired_into_the_gate` passes. The test `a_free_form_question_from_the_reader_is_refused_after_build_reading` goes through the real build_reading. The prefix check uses admission::is_user_addressed, which shares `normalised` with has_addressee.

criteria_check.criterion: `cargo test -p athena-core` passes. New unit tests show that a question like `User: Which greeting: (a) hello or (b) hi? Default: (a).` is accepted. Questions with no `User:` prefix, with no alternatives, or with no default are each refused. A question that says the code answers it is refused. A reading with no question is unaffected.

The 17 corpus cases pass in `corpus_cases_get_the_expected_outcome`.

open_issues: The 3% share is an estimate. The replay at verification measures the real share of newly refused accepted readings.

Stored readings with a free-form question now fail `check_reading_text`. The steward leaves such a proposed job out of the drain until `athena go` re-reads it, which is the existing handling for a reading that fails a check.

checks.rs, briefs/reader.rs and briefs.rs were changed although they are not in the brief's deliverable list. Reasons: refusing_check is defined in checks.rs, and the reader rules line and its pin test belong in the reader brief. None is a governance file.

The reading-tests criterion says the rule is wired into build_reading. It is called from refusing_check, which `read_for` runs straight after build_reading. A direct call inside build_reading would skip replay and the corpus mechanism.
mistakes: The first draft of `labels_in` nested an `if` inside an `if`, which clippy rejected. I fixed it by extracting `label_at`.
learnings: `refusing_check` in reading/checks.rs is the only place a reading check may be called. The corpus tests `no_check_bypasses_refusing_check` and `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` enforce that and need a refusing case for each `step!`.
`CorpusCase.forms` is `&'static [&'static str]`, so table-built cases need a leaked slice, or one literal per case.
Clippy on this toolchain enforces collapsible_if for `if a { if let ... }`, so the label parser was split into a helper.
The Bash tool here allows only cargo, git, ls, chmod, mv and rm; it rejects grep, tail, sed, redirects outside the working copy and `$?`.
desires: A way to see the share of past accepted readings that carry a question, to replace the 3% estimate with a measured figure before verification.
grep, head and shell redirects to a file inside the working copy, to read long cargo output without scanning all of it.
